It is used in 214 already and does not create confusion. We are OK with the initial CR of just updating the “i” to “1000+i”. Huawei/HiSilicon | The isolated impact analysis in R1-1901660 says there can be confusion in some cases. Similar to FL, we think this is rather an editorial issue with no functional change, as summarized in R1-1901614. For the further change suggested by FL (from ‘SRS port’ to ‘antenna port’), we prefer to keep the current specs, as the SRS port has been defined in Section 6.2 of 38.211 and is used throughout 38.214. In addition, about PT-RS port indexing, we suggest to add PT-RS under 1000 serious in Section 6.2/7.2 of 38.211 (as PT-RS is embedded in PDSCH/PUSCH), but are also open to discuss other options. Ericsson | As a response to Huawei, there is no definition of “SRS port’” in Section 6.2 of 38.211. Only antenna ports are defined, some are used for transmitting PUSCH others for SRS, but the name “SRS port” is not defined. In 38.214, SRS port is used but there is no definition. The correct name should be “antenna port used for SRS transmission” in 214. A CR adding antenna ports used for PT-RS to 38.211 is a good suggestion. Intel | Our understanding is that there would be no functionality change for the CR. We think FL’s wording the best one. This is not critical, or even may not be an issue. “SRS port 0” = “the first SRS port” = “antenna port 1000”. Since there are many CRs for other issues with functionality change, we suggest deprioritizing such kind of CRs. If time permits, we can discuss it. Samsung | Agree in principle and fine with Ericsson’s updates on SRS ports. Regarding similar issue with PT-RS, should the port number for PT-SR start from 1000 to be aligned with antenna ports for PUSCH? vivo | Fine with Ericsson’ proposal to add PTRS port in 38.211.

Observation 2 There is no definition of ‘coherent antenna port groups’ in the RAN1 specs, although coherent UL MIMO operation applies within antenna port groups according to the RAN1 specs. Observation 3 Whether a value ‘first’ or ‘second’ for tpmi-FullPwrCodebook2-r18 refers to antenna port group 0 or 1 is not stated in 38.306, although one *may* guess that ‘first’ refers to antenna port group 0. Observation 4 While the UE can determine which TPMIs are associated with a port group, 38.306 and the RAN1 specs do not state that all TPMIs associated with a port group must deliver full power. Observation 5 The current specification’s description using only antenna port groups to define TPMI groups may require the UE to report full power Mode 1 TPMIs, and so is insufficient/incorrect. Based on the discussion in the previous sections we propose the following: Proposal 1 Explicitly state which precoders correspond the values ‘first’ or ‘second’ for tpmi-FullPwrCodebook2-r18 in 38.306 Proposal 2 Define two groups of 8 Tx full power Mode 2 precoders/TPMIs for FG 40-7-1g-2 that correspond to ‘first’ and ‘second’ antenna port groups for ranks up to 4, where the full power precoders constitute a single non-zero submatrix in the intermediate precoder matrix from 38.211, using the text proposal given in Annex A. Proposal 3 Update component 3 in 45-3a to “Maximum number of MAC-CE activated joint LTM TCI states across candidate cells and serving cell TCI states across serving cells” Proposal 4 Update component 4 in 45-4a to “Maximum number of MAC-CE activated DL LTM TCI states across all candidate cells and serving cell DL TCI states across serving cells” Proposal 5 Update component 5 in 45-4a to “Maximum number of MAC-CE activated UL LTM TCI states across all candidate cells and serving cell UL TCI states across serving cells” Proposal 6 Include more candidate values for component 3 in FG 45-3a, component 4 in FG 45-4a and component 5 in FG 45-4a. Proposal 7 Clarify that “across all serving cells” means “across all serving cells in the band”. Proposal 8 A UE that supports FG 45-1a can perform L1 measurements on any band.

case of high mobility, e.g., in v=120km/h. Proposal 3: Together with NR-SSS, the sequence-based NR-DMRS/TSS should be considered to improve the channel estimation of NR-PBCH demodulation. Transmission schemes and the number of antenna ports We assume the NR-SSS has same number of antenna port(s) as NR-PBCH and the NR-SSS is sent on the same antenna port as that of NR-PBCH. Assuming same tx power and 2x2 antenna configuration, different transmit diversity are compared based on simulation. Alt.1: Two antenna port based SFBC Alt.2: Single antenna port based transmission scheme In Atl1, the channel estimation uses the NR-SSS+NR-DMRS/TSS designed for 2 antenna ports. But in Alt2, the channel estimation uses the NR-SSS+NR-DMRS/TSS designed for 1 antenna port. The use of tx diversity schemes is transparent to the UEs, which only observes single radio link with equivalent combined channel. In the simulation, we apply precoder cycling across SSS and PBCH symbols within each radio frames and change the precoder cycling parameters over multiple radio frames, such as [1 1]T, [1 -1]T, [1 j]T, [1 –j]T. The different tx diversity schemes are compared in Figure 3-(a) under channel delay spread of 100ns and 1000ns on 4GHz, and in Figure 3-(b) under channel delay spread of 100ns on 30GHz frequency, respectively. The SISO performance is also given as a reference. The other detailed simulation assumption is given in Appendix A. In Figure 3, we use the IFDM of PBCH and DMRS/TSS multiplexing as illustrated comparison. The coherent combining over 40ms TTI for PBCH is used for the analysis of the worst-case in terms of coverage. Since the 2-port SFBC requires orthogonal RS to get respective channel estimation on each antenna, Alt1 performs worse than Alt2 due to higher channel estimation error for NR-PBCH demodulation. (a) 4GHz (b) 30GHz Figure 3: BLER performances of NR-PBCH with various Tx schemes Proposal 4: Transparent tx diversity scheme on 1 antenna port (e.g., precoder cycling) is used for NR-PBCH transmission. Periodicity and coding rate of NR-PBCH demodulation In LTE design, the MIB uses a fixed schedule with a periodicity of 40 ms and repetitions made within 40 ms. The first transmission of the MIB is scheduled in subframe #0 of radio frames for which the SFN mod 4 = 0, and repetitions are scheduled in subframe #0 of all other radio frames. MIB is self-decodable per transmission, but UE is allowed to decode the MIB across the repetitions. Considering the four-time repetitions, the PBCH coding rate is 1/48. A similar principle can be considered for NR as well. Proposal 5: The NR-PBCH periodicity is [40]ms and the coding rate of NR-PBCH considering repetitions within the NR-PBCH window of [40]ms shall be around 1/48.

Sanya, China, 16th – 20th April 2018 Agenda Item: 7.1.2.3.7 Document for: Discussion and Decision Proposal In LTE, a description of the boundaries in frequency and time within which the inference of channels from one RE to another RE on the same antenna port may be applied. Hence, in Section 6.2.1 of TS 36.211, there is a description for MBSFN RS, DMRS for PDSCH and EPDCCH, CSI-RS and for PRS. The same description needs to hold also for NR but currently the specification text is missing. As proposed in [1], the antenna port definition in TS 38.211 should have constraints on applicability of the antenna port assumption for DM-RS and CSI-RS across time and frequency resources. In this contribution, we formalize the description by defining, for each antenna port, which time and frequency resources the antenna port is valid for. This set of REs will then define a region, labelled as the port coherency region. Hence, we propose the following modifications to TS 38.211. <<<<<<<<<< Text proposal for TS 38.211 >>>>>>>>>>> 4.4.1 Antenna ports An antenna port is defined over a set of resource elements in time and frequency, the port coherency region, such that the channel over which a symbol on the antenna port is conveyed can be inferred from the channel over which another symbol on the same antenna port is conveyed if both symbols are within the port coherency region. - For a DM-RS port associated with PDSCH, the port coherency region is defined as the OFDM symbols of the scheduled PDSCH and within the PRG containing the DM-RS as described in Clause 5.1.2.3 of [TS 38.214] - For a CSI-RS port, the port coherency region is the resource elements used by the port of the CSI-RS resource in a single slot when the channel measurement restriction is enabled as described in Clause 5.2 in [TS 38.214] and the resource elements used by the port of the CSI-RS resource across an unrestricted set of slots otherwise. Two antenna ports are said to be quasi co-located if the large-scale properties of the channel over which a symbol on one antenna port is conveyed can be inferred from the channel over which a symbol on the other antenna port is conveyed. The large-scale properties include one or more of delay spread, Doppler spread, Doppler shift, average gain, average delay, and spatial Rx parameters. [1] R1-1802405 “Corrections to QCL for NR” Intel Corporation

This contribution has examined design issues related to NR system information delivery in initial access, and made the following observations and proposals. Proposal 1: Consider Table 1 as a starting point for potential contents of NR-PBCH. Proposal 2: The NR-DMRS/TSS IFDMed with NR-PBCH should be considered to indicate the NR-SS block indices. Proposal 3: Together with NR-SSS, the sequence-based NR-DMRS/TSS should be considered to improve the channel estimation of NR-PBCH demodulation. Proposal 4: Transparent tx diversity scheme on 1 antenna port (e.g., precoder cycling) is used for NR-PBCH transmission. Proposal 5: The NR-PBCH periodicity is [40]ms and the coding rate of NR-PBCH considering repetitions within the NR-PBCH window of [40]ms shall be around 1/48.

{"chunk_id":"R1-2501941-004","collection":"ran1_tdoc_chunks","metadata":{"source":["Ericsson Japan K.K"],"tdocNumber":"R1-2501941","title":"Remaining issues for 3 Tx UL transmissions"},"point_id":"351832295376335626"}
he higher-layer parameter usage set to ‘codebook’ or ‘antennaSwitching’. Further, the codebook selection criteria should be clarified for 3 Tx operation in Section 6.1.1.1 (‘Codebook based UL transmission’). This is required since the legacy specification selects the precoder based on the higher layer parameter nrofSRS-Ports or nrofSRS-Ports-n8 in SRS-Config, which for a 3 Tx codebook based transmission is 4, i.e., the network configures 4-port SRS resource(s) for 3 Tx codebook based operation. Accordingly, to align with Section 6.3.1.5 in TS 38.211, the following clarification should be included in Section 6.1.1.1. When [RRCparameter] is configured to ‘disable port 1003’, the UE behavior should be clarified in Section 6.2.1 (UL sounding procedure) of TS 38.214 to explicitly indicate that the UE does not transmit on port 1003. Additional clarification may also be added to restrict the [RRCparameter] configuration to SRS resource sets with usage set to ‘codebook’ and ‘antennaSwitching’. Additional clarification is needed in Section 6.1.1.1 (Codebook-based UL transmission) of TS 38.214 regarding the selection of precoders for 3 Tx PUSCH. The legacy specification selects the precoder based on the number of antenna ports equal to either nrofSRS-Ports or nrofSRS-Ports-n8 in SRS-config, which equals 4 for 3 Tx operation. Therefore, it should be explicitly clarified that when [RRCparameter] is configured, the precoder is selected from a codebook with 3 antenna ports. Confirm the following enhancement in Section 6.2.1 of TS 38.214 to clarify the UE behavior when [RRCparameter] is configured to disable port 1003, where [RRCparameter] is only configured for SRS resource set with usage ‘codebook’ and ‘antenna switching’: The UE does not transmit SRS on antenna port 1003 if [RRCparameter] is configured in SRS resource set(s) with higher layer parameter usage set to ‘codebook’ or ‘antennaSwitching’. Include the following enhancement in Section 6.1.1.1 of TS 38.214 to clarify that the precoder is selected from the uplink codebook with the number of antenna ports equal to 3 when [RRCparameter] is configured: The transmission precoder is selected from the uplink codebook that has a number of antenna ports equal to higher layer parameter nrofSRS-Ports or nrofSRS-Ports-n8 in SRS-Config, if [RRCparameter] is not configured, or 3 if [RRCparameter] is configured, as defined in Clause 6.3.1.5 of [4, TS 38.211].

In previous meeting, the following agreement was made: Agreements: In 6.3.2.4.1 of TS38.211, No intra-slot frequency hopping is replaced as higher layer parameter PUCCH-frequency-hopping = “disabled”. Intra-slot frequency hopping is replaced as higher layer parameter PUCCH-frequency-hopping = “enabled”. Add the following: The channel over which a symbol on the antenna port used for UL transmission is conveyed can be inferred from the channel over which another symbol on the same antenna port is conveyed only if the two symbols correspond to the same frequency hop, when frequency hop is enabled, irrespective of whether the frequency hop distance is zero or not. DCM claims that the current description in TS 38.211 is not enough. Similar ambiguity of OCC configuration remains at 6.4.1.3.1.1 in 38.211 for DMRS in PUCCH format 1; when the higher-layer parameter intraSlotFrequencyHopping is provided and secondHopPRB is the same as startingPRB, it is unclear which OCC configuration of “intra-slot hopping” or “no intra-slot hopping” is used. To avoid the ambiguity between gNB and UE, the same sentence as that at 6.3.2.4.1 in 38.211 needs to be added where DCM proposes the following TP. Proposal 5: Adopt the following TP should be adopted in section 6.4.1.3.1 in TS 38.211. Both Panasonic and DCM propose for the replacement of the corresponding text where Panasonic suggests to be moved to section 6.3.2.1 to be applicable for all the PUCCH formats while DCM suggests the description to be moved to section 4.4.1 to be applicable for any UL transmission while. The above text proposal in TS38.211 Section 6.3.4.1, is moved to Section 6.3.2.1 in order to apply all intra-slot frequency hopping of PUCCH. Adopt the following TP in TS 38.211 section 4.4.1. Proposal 6: Discuss whether the following TP should be adopted in section 4.4.1 in TS 38.211. Regarding the corresponding text in TS 38.211, Panasonic proposes some modifications in the text as modifications to clarify that the description is from the Tx side (i.e. UE). Proposal 6: Discuss whether the following TP should be adopted in TS38.211 Section 6.3.2.4.1
